We are an early-stage, venture-backed AI infrastructure company building production-ready Kubernetes-based systems for GPU-intensive workloads. Our platform helps companies go from bare metal to fully operational AI clusters in days, and we're looking for a Java Developer to join our small, high-impact engineering team.

What You'll Do

  • Understand customer requirements and translate them into robust, scalable Java-based solutions.

  • Design, develop, and maintain backend services and infrastructure tooling that supports our distributed systems platform.

  • Collaborate closely with product and infrastructure engineers to deliver features end-to-end.

  • Contribute to the reliability and performance of systems handling AI inference pipelines, distributed training, storage orchestration, and GPU scheduling workloads.

  • Participate in code reviews, architectural discussions, and continuous improvement of engineering practices.

What We're Looking For

  • Required:

    • Solid hands-on experience with Java development and the JVM ecosystem.

    • Familiarity with distributed systems concepts and cloud-native environments.

    • Experience working with or around Kubernetes, containerization (Docker), or related infrastructure tooling.

    • Strong problem-solving skills and ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, early-stage environment.

    • Clear communication skills â we are a small team and direct collaboration matters.

  • Nice to have:

    • Experience with GitOps workflows or tools (e.g., Flux, ArgoCD).

    • Exposure to GPU scheduling, ML infrastructure, or high-performance computing environments.

    • Familiarity with open-source contribution practices.

    • Experience in a startup or early-stage company setting.

Compensation & Benefits

Compensation details were not provided for this role. This is a full-time position at an early-stage, VC-backed company where equity participation is typical. Details will be discussed during the interview process.

Location

This role is based in Los Angeles, CA, USA. The company also has a presence in San Francisco, CA.

Visa sponsorship is not available for this position.

title: Donât Put Yourself a Box
description:
Photo by Piotr MusioÅ / Unsplash

Donât Put Yourself in a Box

Personal Development and Career Growth

  • Apr 26, 2024

Summary

  • Companies need "boxes" (job classifications) to grow and function. This makes hiring, compensation, and career development tractable, and promotes fair treatment of employees.
  • If the boxes are too large, a company can't grow. If the boxes are too small, innovation and ownership are smothered.
  • The size of a company's boxes is directly proportional to the level of trust employees have for management.
  • To get hired, put yourself in the box the company is hiring for. Tailor your resume to highlight those skills and experiences; put yourself out there as a âspecialistâ in the thing theyâre hiring for.
  • If aiming for a promotion, demonstrate how your work embodies the behaviors and impacts of the next-level âboxâ.
  • Don't let those boxes define you. Your value and identity goes far beyond any job description.

Hot Take

Businesses can't function at scale unless they put people in standardized "boxes"; if you want to be hired and to grow your career, you need to understand that, and understand how to work with those boxes. On the other hand, you can't be reduced to a box, and if you tie your identity to those boxes in your thinking, you'll limit yourself in ways that are unnatural and harmful.

This is like the paradox of SchrÃ¶dinger's Cat, both alive and dead at the same time. Like with quantum mechanics and the cat, whether youâre in a box or not depends on whoâs doing the measuring: your employer, or you.

My Box Origin Story

My introduction to the idea of âboxesâ came in the late 2000s, when I noticed that people at Google were having a hard time getting hired or promoted if they were doing âoperationalâ work that didnât involve much traditional program management. Whether they were being considered for hiring or promotion, they were told, essentially, âYouâve done some great work, but itâs not program management; weâre not sure what role/ladder is a fit for you, but itâs not this one. Next!â

This was clearly a problemâeven though they didnât do PERT diagrams and Gantt charts, Googlers did important work in these roles, and roadblocks to hiring and promoting them created both operational and retention issues as jobs went vacant and high-performing employees felt their value wasnât being recognized. As a member of both Program Management hiring and promotion committees at Google I had more visibility to this issue than most others; I spoke to a friend of mine in People Operations (Googleâs HR), who turned out to already be well aware of this problem from repeatedly dealing with upset hiring managers and frustrated promotion candidates. Together, we hatched a plan: to create a new job ladder (job classification) for these âoperationalâ program managers to move to, that was better suited to the type of work they did.

We gathered some data, wrote a proposal, and set up a meeting with the SVP responsible for all engineering at Google. The SVP had been in quite a few meetings Iâd presented to before; I knew him to be not only a brilliant and capable leader, but a genuinely nice guy, too, so I had no worries about the meeting. Imagine my shock then, when this âgenuinely nice guyâ started yelling at us, telling my partner and I that we were going to wreck Google culture!

I vividly remember what he said: âDONâT PUT PEOPLE IN BOXES!â He told us Google needed some job classifications, but that our culture required those classifications to be both broad and vague so both employees and their managers wouldnât be blocked from doing whatever needed to be done. The worst thing we could do, the SVP told us, was to make the classification âboxesâ so small people could say âthatâs not my jobââwhich is precisely what he saw us proposing to do!

A year or two before this Google had shifted from having just three job types (over-broadly, they were âengineersâ, âtechnical people that donât do engineeringâ, and âeveryone elseâ) to having around around a dozen (one of which was my ladder, âTechnical Program Managersâ). There had been a lot of debate about whether those boxes were already too smallâ¦ but the senior team had decided 12â15 job categories were acceptableâenough large boxes to make hiring, career development, and compensation more efficient, but not so many that jobs were defined too narrowly. We left his office dejected, but also enlightened: it said a lot to me that this SVP thought it so important to Googleâs culture, a lesson Iâve never forgotten. (Times have changed though; Google now has many more job ladders, including at least 5â10 âoperationalâ ladders broken off from Program Management well beyond what my friend and I had proposed).

Why Companies Need Boxes

Why do we need âboxesâ (job classifications) at all? Wouldnât the world be better if everyone just did whatever they saw that needed doing? The value of boxes to corporations comes down to two things: scaling and trust.

Scaling

If youâre in a small startup, you want employees who can wear many hats, and who wonât feel limited by things like job titles. Because there are so few employees, and because you know everyone personally and need everyone you hire to have an outsized impact, you can afford to put a lot of energy into every individual hiring decision. Compensation planning is pretty lightweight and customized, both because there arenât many people to deal with, and because you want to compensate people based on their contribution to the business, regardless of what their title is. Everyone is a âspecial snowflakeâ.

That changes quickly as your startup growsâyou cross a line where it becomes infeasible to treat every hire as a unique individual, with bespoke hiring and compensation. This is where âboxesâ become necessary: you have to put people into categories, with standards for how hiring, compensation, and career progression work for each boxâitâs the only way you can scale the company. The alternative to this would be to allow an increasing number of managers to continue bespoke hiring and comp within their own areasâ¦ which leads to the second issue, trust.

Trust

Because startups are so risky, the ability of potential employees to trust the founders is a big dealâif they donât appear trustworthy, theyâre not going to attract the kind of people they need. As the company grows, the number of managers that both employees and senior management need to trust grows, too. At some point it becomes too much: employeesâ willingness to âhave faithâ that managers will make fair and appropriate decisions drops lower and lower, so much so that everything will fall apart without the enforced fairness of standardized boxes.

ð¡

The size of the boxes in a company are directly proportional to the amount of trust employees have in management

Labor unions are the endgame for this sort of trust problem. One of the big rallying points for companies trying to avoid unionization is always to try to convince employees that management has their best interests at heart, and can be trusted. As a rule, unions have close to zero trust for management, andâas a direct consequenceâunions often push for the smallest âboxesâ possible: boxes for very narrow roles, subdivided by seniority, and sometimes further subdivided by location. They see this as the best way to ensure fairness in an environment where management canât be trusted at all. This is the ultimate version of the cultural harm my SVP was worried about.

Boxes and Hiring

Scaling and trust drive companies to put employees into standard categories, or boxes. How do those boxes affect hiring, and, understanding this, how can you better âsellâ yourself as a candidate for jobs?

Most companies above startup size need to hire for boxes, for the reasons given above; itâs just too much work to do anything else. It would be wonderful if recruiters, interviewers, and hiring managers had the time to carefully read and savor every resume that came in, and then spend time meeting with every candidate to pull out nuances that didnât come across clearly in their job histories. Thatâs not the world we live in, though; there are too many candidates to get through, and too few hours in the day.

The usual practice is for recruiters to work with hiring managers to identify standard requirements (boxes, again!) that can be used to screen out people and reduce the number of candidates they need to go into more depth with (hiring managers will usually never see any of those dropped candidates). Those standard requirements are typically based on a template used for all jobs of the same ladder and level, extended with custom specs tailored to the particular role being hired for. In the language Iâve been using in this article, the job requirements are a very clear âboxâ, and the screening process only lets through candidates whose âshapesâ fit that box, like a childâs sorting toy.

Source: Flickr user rosipaw, CC BY-NC-SA 2.0

When there are lots of candidates for a tiny number of jobs, the recruiters donât magically get more time to handle the extra candidatesâinstead, they often deal with the overload by tightening the screening criteria even further: that is, by making the boxes smaller.

Behaviorally, the shift from âstartupâ to âbig companyâ, and the shift from rapid growth to slow growth, show up to candidates as employers become increasingly selective. Startups like generalists; big companies like specialists. If there are few people vying for each job, hiring managers won't care as much about past experience; if there are many candidates, theyâll only be interested in people whoâve previously done the same kind job theyâre hiring for. These trends are amplified when business is tough and hiring budgets are thin: hiring managers become nervous about using their scarce headcount on unproven candidatesâthey need people who have already shown success in exactly the job the manager needs done.

ð¡

Iâm writing this in April, 2024, in a time of high interest rates and widespread layoffs in tech, and when there are lots of AI-based screening tools being offered that promise to save recruiters time; you do the math about the current hiring marketâ¦

Besides being lucky, there are two powerful ways to cut through âsmall box screeningâ:

  • Put yourself in the box theyâre hiring for. This means customizing your resume for each job you apply for, or at least for each type of job youâre going after. If theyâre hiring for someone with experience doing X, focus your resume on how youâve been successful doing X (or at least, things like X) in the past. When a recruiter or hiring manager looks at your resume, you want them to jump out of their chair and exclaim: âwow, this person is exactly what weâve been looking for!â
  • Pull a Kobayashi Maru by bypassing the whole screening process: use your network of personal connections to get an introduction to the hiring manager. This is probably the single most powerful thing you can do because it exposes you to the hiring manager as a whole person, instead of a peg that fits in a box.

Boxes and Promotions

A similar situation arises with promotions: the people making decisions about whether you should be promoted or not donât (usually) have the familiarity with you, or the time, to make a customized decisionâ¦ and doing so would create fairness issues. Instead, they look at whether you fit the next-level box. I want to talk about two parts to this: one related to the job ladder, and one related to the level.

Job Ladder

I vividly remember one promotion committee I served on, where we were deciding whether or not to promote an individual who had unquestionably performed at the next levelâ¦ but the work theyâd done wasnât consistent with the job ladder (work classification) they were assigned to. They had delivered amazing business impact through striking personal initiative, leadership, and hard workâ¦ but what theyâd done had nothing in common with the sort of work expected for the job ladder, or âboxâ, they were in. Should we promote them, or not? We debated the question for far longer than weâd spent on any other candidate weâd reviewed, called in HR support to advise us, andâ¦ we couldnât decide. The rules were that âif you canât decide, the decision needs to be ânoââ, so we ended by turning down the promotion and recommending the person for a large cash bonus, instead. Our decision was appealed, and the appeal was denied, too, for the same reason: despite the great work, the candidateâs work was outside the box.

Sometimes the process and people deciding on your promotions will be more amenable to âoutside the boxâ work, but really, regardless of whoâs making the promotion decision, and what their ârules of engagementâ are, your chances of success will be greatly enhanced by you being aware of the box imposed by your job ladder as you go about your work, and as you explain that work to others. To be clear: Iâm not saying to limit what you work onâthatâs the ânot my jobâ problem the SVP at the beginning of the article was talking about! What I am saying is that you should proactively plan how you will describe your work in ways consistent with the box.

For example, if youâre a Program Manager and spent a lot of time creating product requirements (the work of a Product Manager at most companies), when you and your direct manager describe it to others, be sure you both talk about (for example) the work you did to understand what other work was dependent on having the requirements, how you delegated and tracked some of the work on market research, bringing it all together into a single document, how you built consensus on the requirements, communicated them to the engineering team, and then managed scope creepâall things that are part of the description of the Program Management box. This makes it easy for the people who will decide on your promotion to say âHuzzah! They did both the Program and Product Managementâ, instead of saying âThis was great Product Management, too bad theyâre a Program Manager.â

Job Level

Really, this is a topic that deserves (and will get) an article all on its own, but I think itâs relevant to surface it here: in general, higher level jobs arenât just harder/bigger/broader versions of lower level jobs: theyâre different âboxesâ altogether. The next-level behaviors senior people are looking for are often behaviors that arenât exercised much, if at all, at your current level. I think of these as âphase changesâ, analogous to the phase changes water goes through as it turns from solid ice to liquid to gas as you turn up the heat: itâs always the same water, but it looks and behaves differently in each phase. Some of these transitions are more abrupt and noticeable than others, but theyâre definitely there. At Google for example, there are noticeable differences between all levels, but the âphase changesâ are especially acute between levels 5 and 6, and between levels 7 and 8.

The takeaway here is that you can greatly increases your chances of success by understanding what those âphase changesâ are (more senior mentors can be super helpful in this)âwhatâs qualitatively different about the next-level boxâand then work with your manager to proactively plan how you will describe your work in ways that highlight those qualitative differences.

Boxes and You

So after telling you about the importance of âboxesâ, now Iâm going to tell youâ¦ to avoid them!

This sure looks like a paradox, but let me explain!

Weâve been talking about how companies, managers, and recruiters use boxes, and how, because of scaling and trust, itâs just not practical for them to operate in any other way. Weâd hope that they donât make the boxes too small, and that they have good judgment in how they apply themâ¦ but boxes are a fact of life in the world of work.

The place where you should avoid boxes isnât in the workplace, though: it's in your head. Itâs completely natural for peopleâs occupation and organization to become a part of their identityâ¦ but it's harmful to let that go too far: you are not your job, and you are not your job title.

A lot has been written about the psychology of tying oneâs identity to their job, but the thing I want to focus on here is how putting yourself in a box in your own thinking (e.g. seeing yourself as a âProduct Managerâ, as a âGooglerâ, and so on) can mean putting counterproductive limits on your own behavior, and your own thinking about whatâs possible.

ð¡

Youâre much more than, and much more capable than, the box youâre in.

From a career perspective, itâs a good practice to periodically take some time out and take stock of where you are now and how that fits with where you want to go. If you do this sort of self-assessment youâll often decide youâre basically on the right path and just need to make some minor adjustmentsâ¦ but sometimes youâll realize that the path youâre on wonât take you where you want to be, and that bigger changes are needed: maybe you should ask your manager for different responsibilities? Change teams? Change job ladders? Even change companies? All of those require seeing beyond the box youâre in.

Even though you need to describe yourself in terms of boxes to get where you are now, if your own thinking is constrained by those boxes, it will be hard for you to see that maybe the best path for you is quite different from the one youâre on. Maybe you should change teams? Roles? Departments? Even change your city, or your employer? Donât get me wrong: I know plenty of people whoâve been in more or less the same job, in the same place, working for the same company, for many years, and theyâre very happyâ¦ but itâs also common for people stay in the same role because they see that role defining them, instead of just being something they do.

How You Can Bring Order From Chaos, Today

Here are some things you can do now to apply these ideas:

  • If youâre looking for a job now, describe yourself as being well inside the box your potential employer is hiring for: tune your resume to the job youâre going after. You should have a different resume at least for every âclassâ of job, and sometimes for each specific job. It can be hard to do it if youâre going after several types of job at the same time, but your LinkedIn resume needs to support the more focused, specialized resumes youâre using. Make sure you highlight the skills and expertise called out in the job ads youâre applying to, and talk about your skill and experience in that area. No one hires generalists, so donât call yourself one in your resume; instead, describe yourself as a specialist in the very thing your target company is hiring for.
  • If youâre working toward a promotion now, put yourself in the box you want to be promoted to. Ask your manager and mentors to help you understand the heart of the next-level box, and think about how you can describe your work, behavior, and accomplishments in terms of that box.
  • Donât tie your identity to the box youâre in. You are a complete person with a personality, skills, and experience that transcend any mere box, and if you tie up your identity with the boxes other people put you in, you will limit the paths you can take and the things you can accomplish.

What Do You Think?

I'd love to hear about your experiences with boxes! If you're a paid supporter of this newsletter (hint, hint!) you can add comments below.

title: Why do you want this new job
description:
No matter which side of the table youâve sat during interviews, youâve probably heard this question: âWhy do you want this new job?â

In the recent past, Iâve interviewed a few candidates and heard the following answers so far:

  • Iâm not learning much on the current job after itâs been 2-4 years.
  • Iâm looking for something that offers better work-life balance.
  • Iâm not really looking for a job. The recruiters got in touch and I thought Iâd discuss.
  • Iâm looking for more challenging work.

All of the above are valid answers. I think thereâs another perfectly valid answer that candidates seldom mention probably due to the gravity of the interview room situation. Iâve interviewed over a hundred candidates across different companies and am yet to find anyone that mentions: I am not happy with my current salary and benefits compared to my skills

Back to topic of answers. So, when someone answers that they are not learning new things on the job, obviously, youâd be curios to know why and how they have tried to change things. Unfortunately, most candidates simply mention that they are doing repeat work and thereâs not much to learn doing the same thing over and over again. This is where I start feeling a little uneasy. However, I understand that itâs a true statement. If youâre in a similar situation, hereâs some suggestion: read books, and write code based on what youâve read. Then, you can tell a much convincing story that, Iâve forced myself to learn new things and hereâs some proof, but I really want to apply the newly learned skills outside the scope of the âhello worldâ skills.

About work-life balance, I totally hear you. And if your current job doesnât suit what you need out of your life, itâs a perfectly valid reason to look for new opportunities. However, make sure youâre able to clearly set the expectation with your potential employer about what work-life balance means for you. For example, if you canât work over 40 hours a week, or must work from home one-two days a week, itâs best to discuss this even before an interview starts to ensure youâre a good match with the employer.

If you showed up at in interview just because a recruiter got in touch, Iâd say introspect first. Itâs possible that on our subconcious mind you have expectations that the potential of the new job offers you something that you donât get at the current job. So, instead of a passive asnwer that the you simply acted based on the recruiterâs invite, itâs much convincing to see if you can lay down one or two things that you expect from the new job that you donât get at the current job.

About looking for more challenge, it sounds like a cliche unless you can share examples of work that is of challenging to you. May be you like the challenge of using more complicated algorithms, may be you like dealing with a lot of data, may be you like supporting production emergencies, but thereâs gotta be something that you can explicitly mention as challenging. It helps employers to understand if theyâre able to provide you with enough challenge on the job.

Finally, if youâre looking for a new job because the current job isnât paying upto the level of your skills and contributions, make sure to communicate it clearly as well. With salaries and benefits, I find it much easier to work with people that know the actual $ figure thatâll make them happy instead of beating around the bush to create confusions all around. Just be confident and tell what makes you happy. If the employer can afford it, most likely theyâll want to get you onboard as a happy employee. If they canât afford it, theyâll do their best. The key here is to be explicit about what you want and be sure and confident about it.

In a nutshell, when you walk into an interview itâs yours to lose. The potential employer is investing their time and resources and would rather have you hired than having to interview other candidates. As long as you are able to justify why you want the new job, theyâll be quite accommodating.

title: Background job monitoring
description:
• Glossary/
  • Scheduled Jobs/
  • Background job monitoring

Scheduled Jobs

Background job monitoring

Background job monitoring is watching asynchronous jobs for timely completion and success signals.

What is background job monitoring?

Background job monitoring describes watching asynchronous jobs for timely completion and success signals. In reliability work, the label is useful only when it maps to a measurable check, a clear owner, and a next action when expectations break. Without that operational meaning, the phrase becomes decoration in dashboards and status updates.

Why it matters

Background job monitoring matters because teams need a precise shared meaning for watching asynchronous jobs for timely completion and success signals. Vague language turns incidents into arguments about words instead of fixes.

When everyone uses the same definition, alerts, status updates, and post-incident reviews stay aligned.

How it works

In practice, watching asynchronous jobs for timely completion and success signals shows up as a concrete signal you can measure or communicate. Operators define what good looks like, watch for deviations, and record what happened when expectations break.

The useful version of background job monitoring is operational: it changes who gets notified, what customers see, or which metric a team reviews after an incident.

Practical example

Imagine a team operating around queue worker heartbeat each minute. When observed behavior stops matching the definition of background job monitoring, the team treats that change as a reliability event with a clear owner and next step.

Common misconception

Background job monitoring requires browser scripting

That reading usually collapses distinct ideas into one slogan. Keep background job monitoring tied to observable behavior so the definition stays useful under pressure.

How Fajita handles this

Use heartbeats or success pings from workers. External HTTP monitors alone may not see queue lag.

title: Resource Manager
description:
Company Description

The Story Shack is a modern, low-overhead creative studio built to scale a brand's story. We give brands the power of an in-house creative team â without the headaches and high costs that plague the industry. We address the broken creative model by offering flexible, budget-friendly, scalable, and specialized solutions for brands.


Role Description

We're on the hunt for a sharp and dependable operator to join our scrappy, fast-growing creative studio and work directly alongside our Head of Community.


As our Resource Manager, you'll be the engine behind the scenes â running talent outreach, supporting creative resourcing, coordinating project needs, and keeping administrative tasks tight and on track. You'll help make sure every project has the right people in place at the right time, and that nothing falls through the cracks.


You'll also get exposure to the business side of a growing agency â supporting resourcing, budgeting, invoicing, and talent relationships as we continue to grow.


If you've got real experience in the agency, studio, or production world, love staying organized amid creative chaos, and want a front-row seat to how a creative company is actually run, this role was made for you.


Responsibilities

  • Manage daily tasks with our 300-person creative community, including administrative outreach to freelance talent such as creative directors, copywriters, directors, cinematographers, photographers, producers, designers, and more â including initial outreach, scheduling, and follow-up.
  • Run availability and rate checks across our talent network for upcoming projects, keeping records accurate and up to date.
  • Support creative resourcing with Project Managers, Account Managers, and Producers by helping match the right talent to the right projects based on skill set, client needs, availability, and budget.
  • Handle financial administration, including invoice monitoring, payment tracking, and flagging discrepancies.
  • Maintain organized, up-to-date talent and project databases.
  • Serve as a first point of contact for talent inquiries and applications, while helping build and maintain strong relationships across our creative community.


Qualifications

  • Experience in a creative agency, studio, or production environment with resourcing responsibilities.
  • Outstanding communication and organizational skills.
  • Comfortable managing multiple tasks and projects simultaneously.
  • Detail-oriented, especially when it comes to financials and scheduling.
  • A collaborative, low-ego attitude with the ability to support someone else's workflow and priorities.
  • Genuine interest in the advertising and film industries and building relationships with creative talent.
  • Familiarity with talent databases, project management tools, and invoicing/accounting software is a plus.
  • Existing relationships within the creative production community are a plus.

title: Projektmanager:in / Innovation Lead (m/w/d)
description:
🌱 Wer wir sind

WasteSide: Mit unserer Plattform bringen wir nachhaltiges Verhalten, Community und echte Brand-Interaktion zusammen.

Unsere Mission: Wir helfen Unternehmen dabei, junge Zielgruppen nicht mit nerviger Werbung zu erreichen, sondern durch echte Aktionen im realen Leben, Umwelt-Challenges und positiven Impact.

Unsere Community: Gemeinsam mit Hochschulen, Brands und Organisationen haben wir bereits mehr als 200.000 Umwelt-Challenges abgeschlossen und über 20.000 Nutzer:innen erreicht.

Unser nächster Schritt: Jetzt bauen wir unsere Projekt- und Innovations-Sparte richtig auf – für die Steuerung großer, wirkungsvoller Initiativen und die Weiterentwicklung unserer Plattform.

Aufgaben

🚀 Was du machen wirst

  • Projektsteuerung im Mehrweg-Bereich: Du übernimmst die operative Betreuung und Steuerung unserer Projekte zusammen mit einer aufstrebenden, größeren Mehrweg-Brand – eine coole Zusammenarbeit, bei der du Kampagnen und White-Label-Anwendungen koordinierst.
  • Steuerung des Innovationsprojekts ("CitySide"): Du verantwortest die Meilensteine und Arbeitspakete unserer KI-gestützten Stadtplattform zur Förderung von nachhaltigem Verhalten und ehrenamtlichem Engagement im urbanen Raum.
  • Fördermittelmanagement: Du übernimmst die Verantwortung für eines unserer Förderprojekte – von Mittelabruf und Budgetüberwachung über fristgerecht erstellte Verwendungsnachweise bis zur Kommunikation mit Fördergebern und Behörden. Dazu gehören auch Recherche und Antragsstellung für weitere passende Förderprogramme (EU, Bund, Land).
  • Stakeholder- & Partner-Management: Du koordinierst die Einbindung lokaler Akteure, Betriebe, Vereine und kommunaler Partner im Rahmen unserer Innovationsinitiativen.
  • Wirkungs- & Prozess-Monitoring: Du behältst Fristen, Projektfortschritte und die messbaren Nachhaltigkeits-Aktivitäten im Blick und sorgst für einen reibungslosen Ablauf.
  • Schnittstelle zum Gründerteam: Du arbeitest eng mit der Geschäftsführung zusammen, bringst eigene Ideen ein und entwickelst unsere Projektprozesse kontinuierlich weiter.
  • Perspektivisch: Übernahme eines zweiten, kundenfinanzierten Projekts inklusive Kundenkommunikation und Reporting.

Qualifikation

🎯 Das solltest du mitbringen

  • Kommunikationsstärke: Du bringst Energie, Struktur und Persönlichkeit in die Abstimmung mit externen Partnern und internen Teams und passt dabei deinen Ton an unterschiedliche Gegenüber an, vom Fördergeber bis zum zahlenden Kunden.
  • Sehr gutes Deutsch: Du kommunizierst sicher und überzeugend auf Deutsch – sowohl im Gespräch als auch schriftlich.
  • Eigenmotivation: Du wartest nicht darauf, dass dir jeder Schritt vorgegeben wird, sondern übernimmst Verantwortung und setzt Dinge selbstständig um.
  • Organisations- & Multitasking-Talent: Du behältst auch bei parallelen Projekten und komplexen Arbeitspaketen stets den Überblick.
  • Startup-Mentalität: Du hast Lust auf Geschwindigkeit, kurze Entscheidungswege, direkte Zusammenarbeit mit Gründer:innen und wenig Konzernpolitik.
  • Erfahrung im Fördermittelmanagement: Du kennst dich mit Förderrichtlinien, Fristen und Verwendungsnachweisen aus – oder hast große Lust, dich da schnell einzuarbeiten.
  • Zahlenverständnis & Sorgfalt: Bei Förderprojekten zählt jede Kostenkategorie – ein ausgeprägtes Zahlenverständnis und hohe Sorgfalt sind hier Gold wert.
  • Erste Erfahrung: Idealerweise hast du bereits erste Erfahrung im Projektmanagement, Eventmanagement oder in der Betreuung von Partnerprojekten gesammelt. Du bringst 2–4 Jahre Berufserfahrung mit, bestenfalls in diesem Bereich.
  • Das Wichtigste: Skills kann man lernen. Entscheidend sind für uns dein Drive, deine Ehrlichkeit und dein Wille, schnell besser zu werden.

Benefits

🔥 Was du von uns bekommst

  • Direkte Zusammenarbeit: Du arbeitest sehr eng mit unserem Gründerteam zusammen und erhältst unmittelbare Einblicke in Strategie, Innovationsmanagement und Unternehmensaufbau.
  • Steile Lernkurve: Du lernst nicht nur einzelne Aufgaben, sondern verstehst, wie große Innovations- und Partnerprojekte von Grund auf gesteuert werden.
  • Verantwortung ab Tag 1: Du bekommst früh eigene Aufgabenbereiche und kannst mit deinen Ideen direkten Einfluss auf unsere Arbeitsweise nehmen.
  • Ehrliches Feedback: Wir geben dir direktes, konstruktives Feedback und unterstützen dich dabei, deine Fähigkeiten kontinuierlich weiterzuentwickeln.
  • Spannende Partner & Themen: Dich erwartet eine coole Zusammenarbeit mit aufstrebenden Brands sowie zukunftsweisenden Plattform-Projekten.
  • Frühe Gestaltungsmöglichkeit: Du hast die Chance, früh Teil von etwas Großem zu werden und unseren Innovationsbereich aktiv mit aufzubauen.
  • Standort-Wahl: Hannover (unser Hauptsitz) oder Heilbronn (unser neuer strategischer Standort mit der Schwarz-Gruppe als Partner) – je nachdem, wo du sitzt.

Warum bist du die richtige Person für unser Team und diesen Job? Erklär es uns - wir freuen uns auf deine Bewerbung!

Account Executive - Nordics - Enterprise
description:
About ElevenLabs

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.

We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $11B - multiples of 11, always.

We have expanded from voice into three main platforms:

  • ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale.

  • ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.

  • ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models.

Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.

How we work

  • High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

  • Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

  • AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

  • Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

  • Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.

What we offer

  • Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

  • Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

  • Learning & development: ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.

  • Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.

  • Annual company offsite: Each year, we bring the entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia and Italy.

  • Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.

We're looking for an experienced, driven Enterprise Account Executive to drive ElevenLabs' growth across the Nordics enterprises. Our ideal candidate has a well-established network and a proven track record of selling to C-level and senior decision-makers at major Nordic organizations - and is passionate about the transformative possibilities of AI voice technology.

In this role you'll act as a strategic partner and trusted advisor, enabling clients to leverage our industry-leading models and ElevenAgents - our end-to-end platform for building and deploying AI voice agents - to reimagine their customer experience, internal workflows, and monetization strategies.

In this role you will:

  • Build and manage a growing portfolio of enterprise accounts across The Nordics

  • Identify new business opportunities where ElevenLabs' conversational AI capabilities - including ElevenAgents - can drive customer engagement, contact center automation, and operational efficiency.

  • Lead consultative, multi-stakeholder sales cycles, building compelling business cases that translate AI voice technology into measurable business value for senior executives and economic buyers.

  • Develop and maintain a deep understanding of the conversational AI landscape, including customer use cases, competitive solutions, and emerging trends - particularly as they apply to regulated Nordics industries

  • Demonstrate expertise - or a strong willingness to learn - about conversational AI and how ElevenLabs' voice technology can unlock value across customer support, virtual agents, IVR modernization, and in-app assistants

  • Develop and execute account strategies to expand ElevenLabs' presence within key enterprise verticals, navigating complex procurement and organizational structures.

  • Partner closely with Customer Success, FDEs and Solutions Engineering to ensure smooth onboarding, deployment, and expansion of accounts.

  • Serve as a trusted advisor to clients, educating C-suite and senior operations leaders on emerging trends in generative AI, voice interfaces, and conversational agents.

Requirements:

  • 7+ years of quota‑carrying enterprise sales experience in SaaS or technology, ideally with exposure to AI, generative AI, LLM-based products, or API‑driven platforms.

  • Proven success closing deals and managing long, complex sales cycles with multiple stakeholders across business, IT, legal, and procurement.

  • Well-connected in the Nordic enterprise landscape, with an existing network of senior individuals and strong executive presence and ability to build relationships at the C‑suite and board level.

  • Experience selling technical solutions to product and engineering leaders; ability to translate complex technology into business value.

  • Deep understanding of enterprise procurement and legal processes in the Nordics, with the ability to accelerate deal velocity within complex organizational structures

  • Comfort operating in an early‑stage, high‑growth environment, including building new playbooks and iterating quickly.

  • Passion for voice and audio AI and how it can unlock transformative value for customers.

  • A hybrid of customer & product-driven mentality that prioritizes client satisfaction & scale

  • Native or full professional proficiency in English. Swedish preferred language skill; strong English for internal collaboration

Location

This role is remote but Stockholm is preferred.

title: Forward Deployed Engineer
description:
About Waniwani

Waniwani builds the infrastructure that distributes insurance and banking products through AI assistants. We raised an $8M seed led by Seedcamp and work with large European banks and insurers. Each enterprise deal has to be scoped, architected, and deployed into a regulated environment. This role owns the layer between a signed deal and a live deployment.

The role

  • Customer workshops, discovery, and requirements (35%). Run technical discovery and workshops with each client, and translate their needs into clear, buildable product requirements for our sales, ops, and engineering teams. Flag what we need to build to support a given setup, such as client self-hosting.

  • Solution architecture and documentation (35%). Design the end-to-end MCP flow and integration architecture for each client, including hosted versus on-premise scenarios, and produce the technical documentation enterprise clients require (BPI France alone is roughly 50 docs).

  • Procurement, security, and delivery oversight (30%). Use our existing compliance library (SOC 2 program, DPAs, prior questionnaire answers) to complete security questionnaires, handle security committees and data-residency questions, and drive procurement to completion. Oversee the MCP deployment itself, which our freelancer network implements.

Across all three, you build the reusable kit that makes this repeatable: scoping templates, architecture patterns, and a procurement answer library.

Objectives

  • 90 days: own scoping and procurement response for active deals, with the reusable kit used on at least one live deal end to end.

  • 6 months: run the full signed-to-live pipeline, including architecture decisions and procurement ownership, without founders in the critical path.

  • 12 months: a repeatable delivery process with patterns reused across clients, and a case for the first hire under this role.

Requirements

  • You are technically credible: you read code, reason fluently about integrations and the MCP and agent stack, and can scope and oversee a deployment. This is not a hands-on production-coding role; implementation is handled by our freelancer network.

  • You are comfortable leading technical conversations with enterprise clients.

  • You can drive a security questionnaire or procurement process to completion from existing documentation.

  • You have worked in or near regulated industries (finance, insurance) and understand compliance and data residency requirements.

  • You work well in ambiguity across sales, ops, and engineering, and ramp into new domains quickly.

  • You have an interest in the MCP and agent stack.

  • You are open to traveling from time to time across Europe and the US to meet clients.

What this role is not

  • A backend engineering role. You will work with clients most of the week.

  • A pure pre-sales role. You own architecture, requirements, and delivery oversight, not only the pitch.

  • A slideware role. You need real technical depth, even though you are not writing production code day to day.

Practicalities

  • Remote-first, based in Europe. Expect travel roughly once a month, primarily Paris, London, and Madrid, with US travel around the 6-month mark. Being able to come to Paris occasionally is a plus but not required.

  • First hire in this function, working directly with the founders and the engineering team.

Process

  • Intro call with our talent partner.

  • 30-minute conversation with Max, our CTO.

  • Work sample based on a real client scenario (live session): scope the flow, draft the architecture, and handle a mock procurement Q&A.

  • Discussions with Robin, our CEO, Luiza, and members of the tech team.

  • Reference checks.

title: (Junior) Energy Data Scientist – Energiedaten & Automatisierung (MSB) (m/w/d)
description:
Über uns

Bei VREY bauen wir das EnergyOS für Mehrfamilienhäuser.

In Deutschland stehen über 3,3 Millionen Mehrparteienhäuser – und sie sind das schwarze Loch der Energiewende. <1% Solardurchdringung. <2% Smart Metering. Kaum Flexibilität oder intelligentes Energiemanagement.

Gleichzeitig zwingt die Regulierung Eigentümer zu massiven Investitionen: Solar wird zur Pflicht, Smart Meter müssen in den nächsten 5 Jahren flächendeckend ausgerollt werden, Heizung und Mobilität elektrifizieren sich. Das Mehrfamilienhaus wird vom Betongold zum aktiven Teil der dezentralen Energieinfrastruktur.

Was fehlt, ist ein integriertes System, das diesen Wandel wirtschaftlich und operativ beherrschbar macht.

VREY kombiniert zertifizierten Messstellenbetrieb mit eigener Software und ermöglicht Eigentümern erstmals, ihren selbst erzeugten Solarstrom direkt an ihre Mieter zu verkaufen – einfach und ohne selbst zum Energieversorger zu werden (§42b EnWG).

Damit wird regulatorischer Zwang zu einer profitablen und planbaren Chance:

  • Zweistellige Renditen und Wertsteigerung für Eigentümer,

  • ~20 % Stromkostenersparnis für Mieter, und

  • digitale Infrastruktur für Speicher, Wärmepumpen und Flexibilität.

Bereits heute betreuen wir eine dreistellige Anzahl an Projekten - darunter die größten Bestandshalter und Wohnungsbaugenossenschaften - in allen 16 Bundesländern. Damit gehören wir nach kürzester Zeit zu den führenden Anbietern im Markt.

Im Zuge unserer Seed-Finanzierung haben wir 3,3 Mio. € von führenden Impact- und Energy-VCs (u. a. Rubio Impact Ventures, HTGF, Kopa Ventures) eingesammelt. Mit dem frischen Kapital gehen wir in die nächste Wachstumsphase und bauen unser Team gezielt aus.

Wir stehen am Anfang eines strukturellen Marktumbruchs. Wer heute die Energieinfrastruktur im Mehrfamilienhaus definiert, prägt sie für Jahrzehnte. Werde Teil von VREY und baue mit uns das führende EnergyOS.

 

Dein Profil

  • Du hast bereits erste Erfahrungen im Consulting (Tier 1/Tier 2), High-Growth Start-ups (idealerweise Operations oder Prozessoptimierung), oder im Projektmanagement gesammelt und ein abgeschlossenes Studium in einem relevanten Bereich

  • Erfahrung oder starkes Interesse an Datenanalyse, Automatisierung und KI/LLM-Agents (z. B. Python, APIs, Umgang mit größeren Datenmengen)

  • Sehr gutes Zahlen- und Datenverständnis; Freude daran, Datenqualitätsprobleme systematisch und datenbasiert zu durchdringen

  • Idealerweise Erfahrung in der Energiewirtschaft / Marktkommunikation (MaKo, Messstellenbetrieb, GGV/Mieterstrom, Bilanzierung) - oder die klare Bereitschaft, sich schnell tief einzuarbeiten.

  • Strukturierte, gewissenhafte Arbeitsweise: du gibst dich nicht mit „Job abgeschlossen" zufrieden, sondern prüfst, ob das Ergebnis inhaltlich stimmt

  • Eigenverantwortung und Ownership-Mentalität: du übernimmst einen Bereich, statt nur Aufgaben abzuarbeiten; und strebst danach, dein volles Potenzial in diesem Bereich zu entfalten

  • Du suchst bewusst keinen 9-to-5-Job, sondern willst in einem schnelllebigen, gründer-nahen Umfeld Verantwortung übernehmen, Strukturen aufbauen und das Wachstum aktiv mitgestalten

  • Du bist in Berlin (oder bereit umzuziehen) - unser Büro ist unser Homebase

  • Du sprichst Deutsch und Englisch fließend

 

Deine Aufgaben

Mission der Rolle

Du sitzt an einer unternehmenskritischen Schnittstelle: tief drin im operativen Energiedaten-Geschäft und mit dem Mandat, dieses Geschäft durch eigene Datenanalysen, Tools und KI-Agenten grundlegend zu automatisieren. Du siehst den unmittelbaren Effekt deiner Arbeit - jedes gelöste Ticket bringt ein Projekt näher an die Abrechnung, jeder gebaute Agent spart dem ganzen Team Zeit.

1. Datenanalyse & Automatisierung durch eigene KI-Agents

  • Du analysierst Messwerte, Zählerstände und Versandjobs auf Muster, Ausreißer und wiederkehrende Fehlerursachen

  • Du übersetzt dieses Wissen in KI-Agenten, die Fehler eigenständig diagnostizieren und Lösungswege vorschlagen oder umsetzen

  • Du bist der fachliche Motor der Messstellenbetrieb (MSB) App: du erkennst aus dem Tagesgeschäft, welche Features fehlen, spezifizierst sie und bringst sie mittels eigener Entwicklung ins Produkt

2. Operative Energiedaten-Verantwortung bis zur Abrechnungsreife

  • Du bringst Projekte Monat für Monat zur Abrechnungsreife: fehlende oder unplausible Messwerte korrigieren, Ersatzwerte über Referenzprofile bilden, Werte maskieren und neu berechnen lassen

  • Du legst Versandjobs an, überwachst deren Status und plausibilisierst die Daten nach jedem Fix

  • Du arbeitest dabei täglich in der App unserer Partner und unserer internen MSB App entlang der marktüblichen MSB-Prozesse

3. Ownership & Skalierung des MSB-Bereichs

  • Du verantwortest alle Energiedaten-Tickets intern (Projekt- und Abrechnungsteams) wie extern (VNB, Lieferanten, ÜNB) - von Annahme über Priorisierung bis Lösung - und bist Eskalationsinstanz bei komplexen Fällen

  • Du behältst die MSB-relevanten Postfächer im Blick, ordnest Nachrichten von Marktpartnern den richtigen Vorgängen zu und stellst sicher, dass keine fristrelevante Kommunikation untergeht

  • Du lernst Praktikant:innen und Werkstudent:innen in Prozesse, Tools und die MSB Bibel ein, begleitest sie bis zur Eigenständigkeit und hältst die Doku aktuell

 

Benefits

Verantwortung: zentrale Rolle in unserem Kernteam

Vergütung: Kompetitives Gehalt und Anteile am Unternehmen

Startdatum: so bald wie möglich, unbefristet

Team & Benefits: Lustiges Team, Tech Budget von 2 Tsd.€, regelmäßige Team Events und Learning Lunches, Gratis Getränke, Deutschlandticket

Weitere Vorteile: Tägliche Zusammenarbeit mit den Gründern, Getränke & Snacks, Personalverantwortung und die Möglichkeit, das Unternehmen von Grund auf mitzugestalten

Das Wichtigste: Du brennst für Unternehmertum und Start-ups. Bei uns entstehen keine endlosen Slide-Decks oder rein theoretische Modelle – wir bauen ein Unternehmen und machen tagtäglich einen großen Schritt nach vorne. Wenn du von Tag 1 an etwas Großem mitgestalten möchtest, bist du bei uns genau richtig.

 

Noch ein paar Worte zum Schluss

title: Senior Performance Marketing Manager Paid Social – Meta & TikTok (m/w/d) · Remote
description:
Das ist dein Job bei uns

Mittwochmorgen. Du öffnest den Business Manager und siehst zwei neue Hooks laufen, deutlich über Benchmark.

Du erhöhst direkt die Budgets. Anschließend briefst du Anna, unsere Creative Strategistin, auf die Iteration der Best Performer.

Anna baut mit Alex, Mona und Tobi aus dem Creative Team ein neues Set. UGC, Founder Ads und mehrere Statics. Wenige Tage später gehen sie live.

Am Donnerstag präsentierst du dem Kunden die Entwicklung der Performance und die nächsten Schritte. Dazu deine Vorschläge für den nächsten Produktlaunch. Rabatte allein reichen dir nicht. Jede Bestellung muss einen positiven Deckungsbeitrag tragen.

Danach briefst du dein Team. Jeder Schritt der Kampagne ist klar verteilt. Am Launchtag knackst du für den Kunden 50.000 € Ad Spend an einem Tag, profitabel.

Genau das ist dein Job.

Wofür wir arbeiten

Wir wollen der stärkste ganzheitliche Wachstumspartner für E-Commerce-Brands im DACH-Raum sein.

Denn was wir immer wieder sehen: Agenturen und Dienstleister betreuen Brands nischig und siloartig, Kanal für Kanal, ohne Blick aufs Ganze. Dabei bleiben enorme Potenziale auf der Strecke.

Wir verstehen uns deshalb nicht als Dienstleister, sondern als Teil des Unternehmens unserer Kunden. Dafür arbeiten bei EVOLVE 30 Spezialisten in sechs Fachbereichen zusammen, vollständig remote und seit dem ersten Tag.

Wir denken Paid Social anders

Dass das Creative über die Performance entscheidet, ist kein Geheimnis mehr. Das ist Standard. Wir setzen zudem eine Ebene höher an und entwickeln conversionstarke Angebote und Funnel mit. Denn ein starker ROAS entsteht selten nur aus guten Ads. Er entsteht aus dem Angebot dahinter:

  • Angebotslogik und Preisstruktur gehören für uns zum Kanal. Jedes Angebot rechnen wir auf Deckungsbeitrag durch, bevor es live geht.

  • Landingpages und Funnels bauen wir mit. Ein Creative verkauft nur so gut wie die Seite dahinter.

  • Creative Strategist, Copywriter, Grafiker und Videografen im eigenen Haus. Kein Warten auf externe Zulieferer, dazu ein AI-Stack für mehr Output.

Genau dafür suchen wir jemanden.

Was dich hier erwartet

Du übernimmst nicht ein paar Werbekonten. Du übernimmst Verantwortung für das Wachstum deiner Kunden über Social Ads und entwickelst eigenständig die richtige Strategie.

Denn wir arbeiten nicht mit Kunden zusammen, um Kampagnen zu verwalten. Wir arbeiten mit ihnen, um sie zum Wachsen zu bringen.

Was das im Alltag heißt:

  • Du planst und steuerst die Paid-Social-Kampagnen auf Meta und TikTok, von der Strategie bis zur täglichen Optimierung

  • Du skalierst Accounts auf hohe fünf- bis sechsstellige Monatsbudgets. Die Zielmetrik ist Profitabilität, nicht Ad Spend.

  • Du entwickelst die Creative-Konzepte mit Anna und dem Creative Team. UGC, Founder Ads und Statics entstehen aus Testdaten, nicht aus Bauchgefühl.

  • Du lieferst die Ideen für Ads und Funnels nach Direct-Response-Prinzipien. Unser Team setzt sie um und arbeitet sie im Detail aus.

  • Du sorgst dafür, dass Hooks, Formate und Narrative laufend getestet werden. Ein Gewinner-Creative hält auf hohen Ad-Spend-Leveln nicht lange.

  • Du führst die wöchentlichen Kundenreportings und berätst auf Entscheiderebene, nicht nur zum Kanal

  • Du baust den Social Ads Bereich weiter aus, über SOPs, Qualitätsmanagement und die fachliche Führung neuer Teammitglieder

Der letzte Punkt ist uns wichtig. Diese Rolle gibt es bei EVOLVE einmal. Deshalb suchen wir jemanden, der die Verantwortung für das gesamte Paid Social Team übernehmen will und sich perspektivisch als Paid Social Lead entwickelt.

Das solltest du mitbringen

  • Mindestens drei Jahre Erfahrung im Performance Marketing mit Schwerpunkt Paid Social, als Hauptkanal und nicht nebenbei

  • Nachweisbare Skalierung von E-Commerce-Accounts auf hohe fünf- bis sechsstellige Monatsbudgets

  • Tiefes Wissen im Meta Business Manager, idealerweise auch im TikTok Ads Manager. Dazu Routine mit Tracking-Tools wie Triple Whale, Admetrics oder Tracify

  • Sicherer Umgang mit Margen, Deckungsbeiträgen, CAC und POAS. Ohne diese Zahlen lässt sich profitabel nicht skalieren

  • Strategisches Verständnis für E-Commerce. Du denkst über den Werbekanal hinaus und steuerst Projekte entlang des gesamten Kundengeschäfts

  • Verständnis für Direct-Response-Mechanismen, UGC-Formate und Founder Ads. Du erkennst, warum ein Creative verkauft, und nicht nur, dass es verkauft

  • Deutsch auf Muttersprachniveau für Kundenkommunikation und Copy-Bewertung. Englisch fließend für die Arbeit in den Ad-Managern

  • Sehr gute Selbstorganisation, auch weil wir 100 % remote arbeiten

  • Idealerweise erste Erfahrung in fachlicher Führung oder im Mentoring von Junioren

Direkt gesagt: Dieser Job passt nicht zu jedem

Du solltest dich nicht bewerben, wenn du keine E-Commerce-Erfahrung mitbringst. Wir suchen jemanden, der Accounts auf exzellentem Niveau steuert. Fachlich challengen wir dich gern. Das E-Commerce-Know-how solltest du jedoch schon mitbringen.

Der Rahmen

  • 100 % Remote seit Tag 1, kein Hybrid-Kompromiss

  • 30 Tage Urlaub

  • Betriebliche Altersvorsorge, Jobrad und Firmenfitness über Wellpass

  • Laptop deiner Wahl und hochwertige Homeoffice-Ausstattung

  • Weiterbildungsbudget sowie Unterstützung durch interne und externe Quellen und Mentoren an deiner Seite

  • Voller Zugriff auf unseren internen AI-Stack

  • Zweimal jährlich Teamevents und Workations

So läuft der Prozess

Deine Bewerbung. Dein Lebenslauf reicht. Wenn wir Rückfragen haben, schicken wir dir einen kurzen Fragebogen.

Erstgespräch. Ein kurzes Video-Gespräch mit Vanessa aus unserem HR: gegenseitiges Kennenlernen, Rahmen und Erwartungen.

Fachgespräch. Hier geht es in die Tiefe, mit der Geschäftsführung oder dem Lead deines Fachbereichs.

Finales Kennenlernen. Mit der Geschäftsführung und deinem zukünftigen Ansprechpartner, persönlich und fachlich. Hier definieren wir deine Stelle noch einmal genau auf Basis deiner Stärken und Interessen.

Entscheidung und Start. Wir entscheiden schnell und planen dein Onboarding gemeinsam.

Deine Entwicklung bei uns

Kurzfristig, die ersten zwei Monate. Einarbeitung in die EVOLVE-Methodik und unsere Prozesse. Du übernimmst erste Accounts gemeinsam mit dem Team.

Mittelfristig. Volle Verantwortung für mehrere High-Budget-Accounts. Du steuerst das Paid-Social-Team fachlich und onboardest ein weiteres Teammitglied.

Langfristig. Du führst als Paid Social Lead den gesamten Social Ads Bereich, fachlich und disziplinarisch, bis zu zehn Personen.

Deine Ansprechpartnerin

Vanessa, unsere HR Managerin, ist dein erster Kontakt und freut sich auf deine Bewerbung.

What you bring

  • Existing network within municipalities, infrastructure, construction, architecture, or related industries is a strong advantage.
  • Fluent German and English communication skills.

Why join?

Lead the growth of an established business with significant market potential.

Enjoy a high level of autonomy and ownership while shaping the commercial strategy for Germany.

Represent an established portfolio of high-quality infrastructure solutions with strong references across Europe.

Join an entrepreneurial, international organization with long-term growth ambitions.

Work in close collaboration with experienced international colleagues while making a direct impact on one of the company's most strategic markets.

Die steigenden Anforderungen der Halbleiterindustrie an leistungsfähigere Chips mit höherer Bandbreite und geringerem Energieverbrauch werden durch unsere Technologie adressiert. Wir ermöglichen die Verbindung von Chips mit Hochdurchsatz-Computernetzwerken bei minimaler Latenz.

Der entscheidende Faktor ist die Nutzung der einzigartigen physikalischen Eigenschaften von Graphen, um elektronische Datenverarbeitung mit photonischer Kommunikation zu vereinen. Dadurch können unzählige Chips miteinander interagieren, als wären sie ein einziges System. Unsere Graphen-Photonik-Innovation hebt Rechenleistung und Effizienz auf ein neues Niveau.

Kurz gesagt: Wir vernetzen Chips zu leistungsstarken, energieeffizienten Systemen und überwinden mit unserer Graphen-Technologie die bisherigen Grenzen der Konnektivität in der Halbleiterindustrie.

CAMPER BUDGET: Du bekommst eine jährliche Freimiete für unsere Camper, damit du den #happyroadsurfing Lifestyle selbst erleben kannst.

DISCOUNTS UND BENEFITS: Nutze unsere Corporate Benefits Plattform, die Travel Industry Card und Family & Friends Rabatte.

DEVELOPMENT & GROWTH: Wachstum spielt eine zentrale Rolle bei roadsurfer! Bei unseren regelmäßigen Station Life Camps und Trainings kannst du dich mit Teammitgliedern aus aller Welt vernetzen und deine Fähigkeiten verbessern – sei es im Bereich Fahrzeugwissen oder Kundenservice – stets begleitet von unseren Learning & Training-Expert:innen.

Deine Rolle – Deine Leidenschaft

  • Du packst mit an, wenn es um die Pflege und Instandhaltung unserer Camper-Vans geht – vom kleinen Handgriff bis zur Vorbereitung für die nächste Reise.

  • Du sorgst dafür, dass unsere Fahrzeuge in Top-Zustand bleiben, indem du einfache Reparaturen übernimmst und alles prüfst, was für einen sicheren Trip wichtig ist.

  • Du dokumentierst Schäden und erledigte Arbeiten sorgfältig, damit wir immer den Überblick behalten.

  • Du stellst sicher, dass alle Teammitglieder Schäden erkennen und korrekt melden, damit nichts übersehen wird.

  • Du findest praktische Lösungen, wenn es mal eng wird zwischen Reparaturen und Buchungen – und hältst den Betrieb am Laufen.

Was du brauchst, um mit uns auf einer Welle zu surfen

  • Lust, mit anzupacken und Dinge in Ordnung zu bringen – handwerkliches Geschick reicht völlig aus

  • Zuverlässigkeit und eine strukturierte Arbeitsweise

  • Spaß an Teamarbeit und klare Kommunikation

Wir ❤️ Transparenz. Das Gehaltsband für diese Position liegt zwischen 32.400 EUR und 34.800 EUR brutto jährlich. title: Head of Sales | Fund Administration | VC & PE | Private Markets (f/m/d)
description:
bunch is building the backbone of private markets. We are enabling next-gen fund operations with one integrated system that combines secure data infrastructure, AI-powered workflows and expert fund services. If you value ownership, growth through real responsibility, and working with a thoughtful, ambitious team, this role might be for you.

Your Role

As Head of Sales at bunch, you will strengthen, lead and scale our sales team across key European markets — UK, Luxembourg and Germany. Reporting directly to the Co-Founder, you will turn our high-touch executive commercial motion into a structured, repeatable sales engine across our key European markets.

You will lead Account Executives and Commercial Associates selling to sophisticated decision-makers across VC, PE, and alternative asset managers (GPs, CFOs, COOs, and Fund Ops teams). Because our business model combines scalable SaaS capabilities with high-touch fund services, sales cycles are relationship-driven, multi-stakeholder, and often long. This role demands a leader who can combine structured organisation and process building, relentless deal execution and strong coaching with domain adaptability.

You will:

  • Lead, coach, and develop Account Executives across UK, Luxembourg and Germany.

  • Set a high bar for sales quality, customer understanding, pipeline discipline, commercial judgment, and performance

  • Define and execute market-by-market sales plans in close partnership with the leadership team

  • Build a predictable sales operating cadence across pipeline reviews, forecasting, deal inspection, CRM discipline, and conversion tracking

  • Set up scalable sales processes across the full funnel — from lead routing, qualification, discovery, mutual action plans, pricing, proposal creation, negotiation, handover, and post-sale feedback loops

  • Own the commercial operating system: CRM hygiene, reporting, dashboarding, pipeline definitions, stage exit criteria, forecasting methodology, activity tracking, and tooling adoption

  • Create and maintain sales handbooks, enablement materials, talk tracks, qualification guides, objection-handling resources, market playbooks, and deal review templates so the team has a clear source of truth

  • Coach the team on complex enterprise sales: discovery, qualification, stakeholder mapping, business-case building, negotiation, pricing, executive communication, and multi-threading

  • Build a regular coaching rhythm through call reviews, deal reviews, pipeline inspection, 1:1s, performance feedback, and structured development plans

  • Stay close to strategic deals where customer trust, market context, executive engagement, or commercial judgment are critical

  • Partner closely with other teams, including Marketing, Customer Success, Product Development, Operations, Legal & Finance, and our Co-Founders to advance commercial outcomes

  • Bring structured market feedback into company planning, including customer needs, competitor patterns, pricing insights, product gaps, and operational blockers

  • Partner with Talent Acquisition to hire, onboard, ramp, and manage performance as the sales team expands

About you

  • You have proven experience navigating commercial models that blend scalable software/SaaS with high-touch services, implementation, or customer operations, understanding how to price, position, and transition complex deals without eroding margins.

  • Extensive B2B commercial experience with proven success closing complex, consultative enterprise software or tech-enabled service deals.

  • Direct experience selling into venture capital, private equity, asset management, or fund services is a strong plus, but your ability to build a high-performing tech sales motion comes first.

  • You have a track record of driving sales motions for high-ticket solutions where deal sizes are consistently in the hundreds of thousands, focusing on relationship-driven, consultative outcomes.

  • You have 3+ years of experience directly managing, coaching, and scaling Account Executives teams, with a clear track record of raising team performance, enforcing pipeline discipline, and driving revenue growth.

  • You have coached team members through long-cycle, multi-stakeholder enterprise deals

  • You have successfully built and scaled sales motions across multiple markets, driving high performance through rigorous CRM discipline, RevOps tooling, and predictable forecasting routines.

  • You excel at creating practical sales handbooks, enablement resources, playbooks, and coaching frameworks that teams rely on to drive complex, long-cycle enterprise deals.

  • You are a seasoned people leader who sets a high bar for excellence, fostering talent through direct feedback, clear performance management, and structured coaching.

  • You combine strong commercial judgment—knowing when to push or qualify out—with the executive presence to build trust and credibility with senior stakeholders.

  • You have a builder mentality and are comfortable creating structure in an environment that is still scaling

  • You communicate excellently in English

Existing understanding of VC / PE fund operations, GP / LP structures, fund administration, investor onboarding, transfer agency, or Luxembourg fund structures is a strong plus.

What success looks like

In your first months, you will build a clear understanding of bunch’s commercial motion, ICP, product, implementation model, pricing, and market dynamics. You will establish trust with the existing sales team, founders, and key cross-functional partners, while introducing a clear cadence for pipeline reviews, deal coaching, forecasting, and performance visibility.

Over time, you will strengthen the team’s execution across priority markets, improve pipeline quality and forecast accuracy, standardise the sales playbook, support hiring and onboarding, and build stronger cross-functional routines with Marketing, Solutions, Operations, Customer Success, Product, and RevOps. You will also establish the core sales infrastructure the team needs to scale: clear funnel processes, reliable CRM workflows, useful dashboards, practical handbooks, repeatable coaching routines, and a shared source of truth for how we sell.

Ultimately, you will help build a high-performing and scalable sales organisation across UK, Luxembourg and Germany, improving predictable revenue generation and constantly raising the quality bar for complex private-markets selling.

Workplace & Benefits

  • Customizable benefits package (wellbeing, sport, mobility, food, and more)

  • 28 days of vacation, plus 2 company days and local public holidays

  • Hybrid setup (3 days/week in office)

  • Up to 4 remote calendar weeks a year

  • A great tech and work setup

  • Work with a diverse team of 120+ bunchies from 40+ countries, with leaders who are best-in-class in their domains

Hiring process

  1. People Team Interview (30 min) – Meet us & check initial fit

  2. Founder’s Interview (60 min) – Role deep dive, sales leadership, and commercial scope

  3. Sales Leadership Case (60 min) – Coaching, pipeline discipline, and complex deal execution

  4. Final Round (3 x 45 min) – Meet our leadership team (Tech, Ops, CS).

  5. In-person Meet & Greet with team members (sellers) and Levent.

  6. Reference checks

About bunch

bunch is building the operating infrastructure for the next generation of private markets. We combine AI-powered automation with deep regulatory expertise to replace fragmented spreadsheets and manual processes with one integrated platform across the fund lifecycle, purpose-built for private markets heading toward $32 trillion in Assets Under Management.

We've 4x our ARR in 2025, crossed 150 fund managers and 12,000 LPs on the platform, and just closed our $35M Series B in May 2026. We're looking for ambitious people who want real ownership of hard problems, and who care about building infrastructure that actually matters to the people using it.

title: Structured Finance Manager (m/f/d)
description:
At Credibur, we are building the infrastructure layer for European private credit: an operating system for non-bank lending that handles borrowing base calculations, drawdown automation, SPV oversight, covenant monitoring, reporting, and backup servicing. Our clients are originators and institutional capital providers across BNPL, factoring, SME lending, leasing, and auto receivables.

If you have spent the last few years inside one lender, one fund, or one asset class, this role offers something different. At Credibur you work across the full spectrum of European structured credit: multiple originators, multiple capital providers, multiple asset classes, simultaneously. Within your first year, you will have touched more deal structures and facility types than most structured finance professionals encounter in five years on a single originator's treasury team.

We are looking for a Structured Finance Manager (m/f/d) to own facility operations across our client base and be the primary day-to-day interface between originators and their lenders. You will work directly with the founding team on live deals from day one.

Tasks

  • Own borrowing base calculation logic: Translate facility documentation into calculation configurations on the Credibur platform: eligibility criteria, advance rates, concentration limits, exception handling. Once live, the platform executes automatically; your job is to design it correctly upfront and manage it as deals evolve.
  • Design asset tape schemas: Define the data requirements for each new client onboarding: which fields matter for the asset class, how originator data maps to Credibur's platform, and where the gaps are. Once configured, ingestion runs automatically; you own the schema design and its ongoing integrity as deals and data sources evolve.
  • Maintain backup servicing playbooks: Define and document operational runbooks for each backup servicing mandate. No prior backup servicing experience required; we will train. What matters is being structured and thorough enough to document processes clearly.
  • Shape the product: Work closely with our engineering team to translate what you see on deals into platform improvements. You are the closest person to how clients actually use Credibur in practice; your input directly drives what gets built.
  • Manage client operations: Handle day-to-day queries from originator treasury teams and lender portfolio managers. Flag issues early, own resolution where you can, and know when to loop in the right people.

Requirements

  • 3 to 4 years of experience in structured finance, warehouse lending, or capital markets operations at a non-bank lender, asset manager, or credit servicer
  • Direct, personal responsibility for producing reports or calculations for an institutional counterparty (not advisory, not purely modeling)
  • Exposure to borrowing base mechanics, eligibility criteria, and asset tape workflows
  • Asset class experience in consumer lending, BNPL, SME loans, factoring, or auto receivables
  • Strong English; able to handle a professional client call independently
  • Nice to have: German language skills (significant plus given our client base); other European languages are a bonus
  • Nice to have: Berlin-based or willing to relocate. Remote candidates from within Europe are possible but Berlin is strongly preferred at this stage.

What We Offer

Unmatched deal breadth at an early career stage

You see how different originators run their facilities, how different lenders and funds approach monitoring and reporting, and how the same mechanics play out differently across asset classes. That breadth is difficult to build anywhere else at this stage.

Direct access to live deals and institutional counterparties

You are not a junior analyst sitting behind a senior relationship manager. You are the operational contact for Heads of Treasury at originators and Lead Portfolio Managers at credit funds.

Founding team proximity

Credibur is early. You work directly alongside the founders on deals that are live and consequential. What you build here shapes how the company operates for years.

Setup

Berlin-based or remote within Europe or UK with travel every few months to our Berlin HQ and/or to clients. No visa sponsorship available.

At Credibur, we believe that diverse teams build better products. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, regardless of gender, age, ethnicity, disability, sexual orientation, or religion. If you're passionate about what we do but don't meet 100% of the criteria, we still encourage you to apply. We value potential and ambition.

All hires complete on-site onboarding in Berlin. Background checks are required as part of our standard compliance process.

Technical

Cross-layer fluency is what lets you pick the right next initiative; it isn't a weekly context-switch.

  • Simplicity / via negativa. Challenge the status quo and remove toil before adding features — automate operational tasks and infrastructure management with Python or Go, reject tools that don't fit the problem, and treat manual on-call work as a defect to be designed out, not a status quo to be staffed up.

Build the agentic setup as a collective surface: humans and digital teammates working as one team, with shared skills, shared context, and shared on-call workflows. Encode recurring infra tasks as internal skills any teammate (human or agent) can pick up and run, so the team's throughput compounds — not just your own.

  • Debugging fluency. Lead incident response, post-mortems, and root-cause analyses — trace failures to the underlying problem (never the symptom), apply the learning back into the architecture, and prevent the same incident from happening twice.

Non-technical

  • Strategic vs. tactical balance. Balance this week's critical work with the 6–12-month platform direction — ship the on-call-driving fix today while shaping the multi-year observability, cost, and reliability investments that move WRITER's enterprise customers.

  • AI in workflow. AI is part of how you ship, not a thing you've read about — agentic tooling (Claude Code, Droid, Codex, internal skills) is in your daily loop, you've built or adopted AI-assisted workflows others now use, and you have strong opinions on where it's unreliable.   • First-principles + decision-making. Demonstrated ability to Challenge the status quo, proactively identify systemic weaknesses, and propose innovative solutions to complex reliability problems — reason from constraints and failure modes (not analogy or vendor defaults), name the tradeoff in business terms (reliability vs. velocity, cost vs. blast radius, standardisation vs. one-off), and reject the "best practices" answer when it doesn't fit the problem.

Non-technical

The way companies innovate is broken. The systems built to create and protect ideas can’t keep up with the pace of change. Today, 90% of S&P 500 company value is intangible (e.g. in intellectual property) - yet R&D and IP teams spend half their time buried in manual work, sifting through patents and paperwork instead of pushing the frontier forward. The tools of creating and protecting are stuck in the past. We’re here to fix that.

Ankar is building the R&D tools for the AI era and defining what applied research will look like in the next 20 years. We’re building infrastructure and product experiences our customers rely on every day. You’ll translate messy, ambiguous problems into clean, dependable software—and you’ll do it at the cutting-edge of AI.

We’re at an inflection point:

  • We’ve raised >$24M to date from Tier-1 VCs like Atomico, Index Ventures, Norrsken, Daphni, and angels like the Founder of Hugging Face, CEO from Datadog, and Leaders from DeepMind and OpenAI.

What you'll be doing

Shape how the world understands our product. Become deeply embedded with Product, Engineering, and our customers to translate complex technical work into clear, compelling narratives that drive adoption, engagement, and commercial impact.

  • Turn product innovation into customer value. Develop clear messaging, positioning, and storytelling that explains not just what we build, but why it matters and the problems it solves.

  • Own product launches end-to-end. Lead the launch strategy for meaningful product releases, from positioning and messaging through internal enablement, customer communication, and external promotion.

  • Drive customer adoption and education. Create product communications, release content, in-product announcements, and educational resources that help customers continuously discover and use new capabilities.

  • Bridge Product, Sales, and Customers. Partner closely with Product, Engineering, Sales, and Customer Success to ensure product developments are communicated clearly, consistently, and effectively across every customer touchpoint.
